newsitem.title: UK: UK union says minimum wage should be set at 4 stg.
newsitem.headline: UK union says minimum wage should be set at 4 stg.

text.p: One of Britain's largest unions, the Transport and General Workers' Union, said on Tuesday the proposed national minimum wage should be set at four pounds per hour.

"The T&G would expect to secure no less than the 4.0 pound ($6.47) per hour rate which we have already negotiated in many instances," union general secretary Bill Morris told delegates at the annual meeting of the British Chambers of Commerce.

He said the Confederation of British Industry appeared to favour 3.50 pounds while the Trades Union Congress (TUC) was still considering what evidence to present to the proposed Low pay Commission which will advise the new Labour government.
Morris said unions did not expect any favours from the new government, despite the long-standing links between the two.
"I don't support the view that the trade unions owe the Labour party anything...and affiliation with the Labour Party does not give us anything special," he said.
A straw poll of delegates at the BCC conference showed unexpected support for his proposed 4.0 stg level.

Over half of the 500 delegates, many of whom represent small businesses which are generally thought to oppose the minimum wage, said they would support four pounds an hour. A smaller number said they would prefer 3.50 stg.
-- Rosemary Bennett, Cardiff Newsroom +44 1222 225430 ($ = 0.617 British Pounds)
